pr_title: Move Ping binary sensor attributes to sensor entities
pr_body:
## Breaking change
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/112004 moved the state attributes to their own entities. Therefore the state attributes will be removed in 2024.10.

To avoid errors in the future when the attributes are removed, users should update all automations and scripts that use the status attributes and utilize the new entities.

## Proposed change
Move the attributes of the binary sensor of the Ping integration to sensor entities. The entities are disabled by default an can be enabled if needed. This way don't store data that is not needed and wanted by the user.

The attributes are kept for backward compatibility and can be removed with version 2024.10.
I don't actually know how the path for deprecation would look like, as I don't know of any way we can determine attribute usage.

~ToDo: Docs~

issue_context.title: Ping binary sensor flooding DB by "round_trip_time" attributes
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This is may be not considered as a "bug" - but this is a serious issue about excessive writing to DB.

Here is a "states" table for one `binary_sensor` entity created by the Ping integration.
It has records for every 60 sec - I switched off a polling and update the entity in an automation every minute.
So, in a default config these records will be written every 30 sec.

![изображение](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/23632185-771d-4c09-83f8-1980890ef4d9)

Difference in records is only in these "round_trip_time" attributes:

![изображение](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/71872483/f22cf5c8-77b9-43dd-87df-7f9308d63ed5)

Strongly suggest to exclude these attributes from DB.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2024.2.3

Thanks for bringing this up. I've moved the attributes to their own entities now, which are disabled by default, this will be released with version 2024.4. However, the attributes will be kept until 2024.7 to be backwards compatible. After that, the attributes will be removed. We cannot simply remove them from the record now as some users may rely on them.

There is also a possible negative side effect of moving attributes to sensors. 
Currently a ping binary sensor have an updated “last_updated” attribute after every ping. So a user can see that ping was made. 
If attributes are moved to sensors - will the “last_updated” still be updated?
If yes:
- this allows us to see “ping was made”;
- but a new record is written to DB - with same state.

This only applies to the attributes of the ping sensor (the `rtt` attributes). `last_updated` is kept (though it is technically not a attribute), as it is not handled by Ping, but by HA and this is how things work in HA

To clarify for myself:
- last_updated - still be updated after every ping
- each ping will create a new record in DB with possibly same state and an updated last_updated 

Right?

Yes, `last_updated` is still being updated, as any other entity also.

No, just state changes (or attribute changes, which are part of the state actually) are written to the history database. So if the state of the binary sensor wont change, no new record will created, but updated, unless you restart iirc.

> No, just state changes (or attribute changes, which are part of the state actually) are written to the history database

This is good. I have some examples with other integrations where a new record is created for same state and unchanged attributes. These records have different las_updated.
Yeah, I'm not 100% sure about that. I'm not that deep into recorder, but it still has nothing to do with the ping integration. It's a general thing with how recorder handles this.

Ok, let’s check it in 2024.7. 
thanks again!!!
